text:
maria: quick question — i'm sketching a refactor to split the orchestration stack. currently everything's in one "coordinator" binary. thinking of an explicit planner (global scheduler) vs agent (per-pool node agent) split. where should eviction/headroom semantics live?
aj: my take: planner owns long-term policy (quota, fairness, global headroom), agent owns immediate decisions (probe, soft-evict when node overloaded). planner gives hints, agent enforces SLOs.
devon: agree with aj. main gotcha is race conditions: two agents evicting the same tenant because planner hasn't reconciled. need idempotent leasing / short lease tokens.
samira: +1. also telemetry surface matters. planner needs per-tenant demand curves (rps, seq len) to make allocation decisions. agents should only emit lightweight signals, not full traces.
maria: concretely: proposal sketch below. agent receives a lease token from planner with expiry and metadata. agent may preempt soft reservations if local pressure > threshold, but must report action back with backoff window.
maria: ```json
{
  "lease": "L-12345",
  "owner_tenant": "tenant-42",
  "expires_at": "2024-11-12T15:02:00Z",
  "headroom": 2,
  "policy": "soft-reserve"
}
```

lee: sounds reasonable. question: where do we evaluate cost tradeoffs (quantize batching vs spinup)? planner has global cost model, but agent has better locality info (cv of startup times). maybe we let agent compute a local_adj factor and report it periodically. planner multiplies by that factor for admission planning.
aj: yeah, local_adjustment is good. keep math simple on planner side: effective_headroom = announced_headroom * local_adj

infra-bot: deploy-check: planner-api v2 will add field `local_adj` to LeaseStatus. Please bump compatibility.
devon: another operational concern: upgrades. if agent is temporarily lagging, we shouldn't have planner push hard decisions that agents can't enforce. need a degraded-mode where planner falls back to capacity-based admission (no evictions).
samira: op note: add an observable: "agent_evicts_total" with labels {tenant, reason, preemptible}. that will let us catch incorrect planner policies.
maria: timeline idea: land planner read-only surface first (expose leases, signals), then agent implements enforcement in canary pool. run for 2 weeks with canaries before turning on planner-initiated evictions.
aj: one more nit: naming. call the short-lived node agent "agent" and the global decision engine "planner"? feels less confusing. :+1:
maria: good catch. i'll rename in RFC draft to planner vs agent.

lee: 👍 also add a simple JSON example of degraded-mode in the RFC: `{ "mode": "degraded", "reason": "agent-mismatch" }`
maria: summary action items:
- switch naming -> planner/agent in RFC draft
- add lease token example + local_adj field (aj)
- add agent_evicts_total metric + alert (samira)
- propose canary rollout plan (maria)
aj: +1 to everything. tagging @devon for the idempotent lease implementation follow-up.
devon: i'll draft the idempotent lease proto and a small test harness that simulates split-brain evictions. aim for PR by EOW.
maria: perfect. thanks everyone. closing thread after the RFC update. :rocket:
